after.zh: 形状只在「匹配」里出现：每张图单看都只是杂点。对应点只需在同一行里找，视差越大，物体越近。
after.en: The shape only appears through matching: each image on its own is just speckle. Corresponding points only need to be searched for along the same row, and the larger the disparity, the nearer the object.

t.zh: 伸出一根手指放在眼前，轮流闭上左眼和右眼：手指和远处的墙，哪个跳得更厉害？同一样东西在两只眼里错开的距离，叫视差。
t.en: Hold a finger up in front of your eyes and close your left and right eye in turn: which jumps more, your finger or the far wall? The distance by which the same thing is offset between your two eyes is called disparity.

t.zh: 机器人和汽车上的双目相机也靠视差判断远近。这一关的两张图都是随机噪点，单看哪张都没有形状；心理学家 Julesz 在 1960 年用这种图证明，人不认出任何物体也能看出立体。
t.en: The stereo cameras on robots and cars also use disparity to judge distance. Both images in this level are random dots, and neither shows any shape on its own; in 1960 the psychologist Julesz used images like these to show that people can see depth without recognising any object.

t.zh: 新原件<part-ref to="part:argmin4"></part-ref>接四张图，逐格看哪一张最小，输出它的编号 0–3。
t.en: The new primitive <part-ref to="part:argmin4"></part-ref> takes four pictures and, cell by cell, outputs the number 0–3 of the one that is smallest.

t.zh: 输出是一张视差图：每格填 0 到 3，表示那里的东西在两张图之间错开了几格，少数格子出错可以接受。要想的是：怎样判断右图的某一格和左图的这一格是同一处？
t.en: The output is a disparity map: each pixel holds 0 to 3, the number of pixels by which the thing there is offset between the two images. A few wrong pixels are fine. The question is: how can you tell that a pixel in the right image is the same spot as this pixel in the left image?

caption.zh: 左图、右图 → 每格的视差
caption.en: Left image, right image → disparity at each pixel

brief.zh: 左右两台相机拍同一个场景。输出每个像素的视差 d（0 … 3）：右图里同一个点比左图往左挪了几格。
brief.en: Two cameras, left and right, photograph the same scene. Output each pixel's disparity d (0 … 3): how many pixels further left the same point is in the right image.

hint.zh: 对每个可能的 d，把右图挪一挪再和左图比。单个像素比不准时，看看它周围。
hint.en: For each possible d, shift the right image and compare it with the left one. When single pixels do not compare reliably, look at what is around them.
